verifications.claim: As of late April 1, 2026, the Artemis II Orion capsule is in high Earth orbit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '8:52 PM / April 1, 2026 Second engine burn completed... raising the high point, or apogee, of the orbit to 43,760 miles — higher than any astronauts have flown since...'; R2: 'An 18-minute, six second engine burn successfully sent Artemis II into a high-Earth orbit.'; R5: 'The craft is currently in a high Earth orbit'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm high elliptical Earth orbit established by late April 1 after apogee/perigee raises.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule had a successful 6:35 p.m. ET launch from Kennedy Space Center.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '6:36 PM / April 1, 2026 Artemis II lifts off Artemis II lifted off at 6:35 p.m. EDT.'; R2: 'launched into the clear sky at 6:35 p.m. Eastern time.'; R6: 'lifted off from Kennedy Space Center in Florida at 6:35 p.m. ET.'
verifications.reasoning: All sources directly confirm exact time and location of successful launch.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew has separated from the ICPS upper stage.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '10:01 PM / April 1, 2026 Orion separates from interim cryogenic propulsion stage'; R2: 'The Orion spacecraft separated from the upper stage of the rocket.'; R5: 'the crew takes manual control of their Orion spacecraft... Having completed its primary objective, the SLS second stage...'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state separation from ICPS occurred post-launch on April 1.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is conducting systems tests.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'put their Orion capsule through its paces'; 'thoroughly test their Orion capsule'; 'check out the Orion capsule, making sure... communications, navigation, propulsion and life support systems'; R2: 'check that the spacecraft can safely make the journey'; R5: 'perform check-out tests'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe ongoing systems checkout and tests during initial Earth orbit phase.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is preparing for a maneuver to send them toward the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'before finally heading for the moon'; 'before pressing out to the moon'; R2: 'On Thursday, Orion will fire its engines to push it on a path toward the moon.'; R3: 'successfully conducting the translunar injection burn, or TLI'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm preparation for TLI burn after Earth orbit tests to head to Moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew consists of Wiseman, Glover, Koch, Hansen.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'commander Reid Wiseman, pilot Victor Glover, mission specialist Christina Koch and Canadian astronaut Jeremy Hansen'; identical in R2, R5, R6.
verifications.reasoning: All sources list exact crew: Wiseman, Glover, Koch, Hansen.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew has completed a perigee raise to lift their orbit's lowest point.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '7:52 PM / April 1, 2026 First engine burn completed... raising the low point, or perigee, of the orbit to a safe 115 miles.'; R5: 'perigee raise, lifting the lowest point in its elliptical orbit'
verifications.reasoning: Direct confirmation of perigee raise burn completed shortly after launch.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II Orion capsule will perform a Trans-Lunar Injection (TLI) burn to set a course for the Moon.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'an engine firing called the "trans-lunar injection," or TLI'; R2: 'translunar injection burn'; R3: 'translunar injection burn, or TLI'; R6: 'translunar injection burn'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources confirm planned future TLI burn for lunar trajectory.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II mission is a 10-day, nine-and-a-half-day journey around the Moon and back.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'about nine and a half days'; R2: '10-day mission'; R3: '10-day mission'; R6: '10-day journey'
verifications.reasoning: Sources consistently describe ~10 or 9.5-day mission looping around Moon.

verifications.claim: The Artemis II crew is reportedly doing well.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'the ascent was an "amazing ride"'; R4: 'The crew is doing well and safely in orbit.'; R5: '“safe, they’re secure and they’re in great spirits”'; R6: 'crew safe, secure, great spirits'
verifications.reasoning: Sources report crew in good condition and spirits post-launch.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is the first crewed flight of the Artemis program.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'first piloted moonshot since... Apollo'; 'Orion... its first with a crew'; R2: 'first time astronauts rode on top of the mighty Saturn V rocket [equiv]'; R4: 'first crewed flight of the Orion spacecraft'; R5: 'first time humans have headed to the Moon since Apollo 17'
verifications.reasoning: All confirm Artemis II as first crewed Artemis mission after uncrewed Artemis I.

verifications.claim: Artemis II is designed to test all systems required for future Moon landings.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'test their Orion capsule... to make sure it's up to the task'; 'capabilities for future missions, including the ability to dock with a lunar lander'; R2: 'check that the spacecraft can safely make the journey and keep its crew alive during trips to and from the moon'; R5: 'proximity operations demonstration is intended to simulate docking with another spacecraft... necessary for future Artemis missions'
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe testing key systems like docking, life support for future lunar missions, but not explicitly 'all systems required'.
